A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Cornstarch by the same authors. All pages, including v1 Appendices A–D and v3 Appendices A–E, are readable and support comparison of the text, equations, tables, and figures despite substantial restructuring.

before.justification: v1 reports original GPU experiments measuring training throughput, pipeline execution, and attention latency in Section 6 and Appendices B–D.

after.justification: v3 reports original training-time comparisons, component ablations, GPU activity measurements, and multistream experiments in Section 7 and Appendices D–E.

M1.justification: v3 retains BAM and inter-GPU LPT scheduling but adds intra-GPU attention subdivision and an aggregation kernel (Section 5.2). Its model-parallelization algorithm selects between colocated and independently parallelized encoders. It also replaces v1's approximate backward-time multipliers with separately profiled parameter-gradient and input-gradient costs. These change execution and partitioning procedures.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate synthetic vision, audio, and text workloads. However, v1's end-to-end coverage includes vision-language, audio-language, and combined vision-audio-language training; v3's main evaluation concentrates on the combined task. Vision-language training remains in v3's motivating experiment, but standalone audio-language evaluation disappears. No new empirical domain is introduced.

E2.justification: v1 evaluates encoder-colocated and encoder-replicated baselines. v3 retains a Megatron-derived comparison as Megatron*, adds FSDP2 and GraphPipe*, and drops encoder replication. Context-parallel comparisons also replace separate naive-ring and random-distribution entries with inter-only, intra-only, combined, and multistream comparisons (Table 3 and Appendix E).

E3.justification: On the same 24-A40 testbed, v3 replaces EVA-CLIP/Whisper configurations with Qwen2 Vision/Phi4 Audio configurations, changes audio duration from 30 seconds to two minutes, and changes pipelined batches from 24 single-sample microbatches to 12 microbatches of four samples. End-to-end reporting changes from throughput per GPU to iteration time. Context experiments replace the specified 70B attention-layer setup with small/medium/large LLM configurations and whole-model measurements.

E4.justification: Frozen-status and encoder-placement ablations are retained but redesigned. v3 adds separate inter-GPU and intra-GPU balancing ablations, compute-unit activity analysis explaining stragglers, and a multiple-CUDA-stream alternative (Section 7.4 and Appendix E). These substantially extend the mechanism analysis beyond v1's token-distribution timings and sampled per-rank comparisons.

E5.justification: v1 Section 6.5 specifies 50 runs per attention-mask type, newly randomized masks, and averaged timings. v3's corresponding context experiments omit a repetition count and comparable averaging description. This is a reporting removal, not evidence that fewer runs occurred. Neither version supplies confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: The main and appendix result sets are substantially replaced. v1 reports up to 1.57× end-to-end throughput improvement; v3 reports 2.26× on average under changed settings and baselines, so these are not directly comparable gains. v3 Table 3 newly reports LLM-L attention times of 568.18 ms for causal CP, 610.67 ms for inter-only balancing, and 551.60 ms for combined balancing.

T1.justification: v3 Section 4.3 replaces v1's 0/1/2-times-forward backward-cost approximation with a parameter/input-gradient decomposition and recursive trainability propagation. Section 4.4 adds reasoning for activation memory and in-flight microbatches in graph-shaped pipelines. The makespan ILP and LPT bound remain, while v1's Chernoff-based random-distribution discussion is removed.

C1.justification: The contribution framing shifts from modular construction and a novel modality-parallelism dimension toward previously neglected higher-order heterogeneity, refined frozen-aware partitioning, and joint inter-/intra-GPU balancing. Modality parallelization is now positioned as combining existing strategies. The headline performance claim also changes from a maximum 1.57× improvement to a 2.26× average over the revised evaluation.

C2.justification: v3 explains why balancing total work across GPUs can still leave compute-unit stragglers, and discusses subdivision, aggregation, and multistream tradeoffs. It also explains when encoder colocation helps and why extreme module-size disparities can prevent frozen-aware partitioning from improving performance. These substantially extend v1's explanations based mainly on pipeline bubbles and per-GPU workload balance.

D1.justification: v3 adds an explicit code-repository link, revised API usage, separate gradient profiling, Triton attention implementation details, and subblock guidance. Software documentation changes from PyTorch nightly/Colossal-AI 0.4.4 to PyTorch 2.6.0, Transformers 4.51.0, and Colossal-AI 0.4.6. Conversely, v1's callback example and detailed per-model parallelism configurations in Tables 5, 6, and 9 are absent; their removal does not establish that callback functionality was removed.

R1.justification: v3 substantially expands positioning around distributed multimodal training, adding substantive discussion of DistTrain, Optimus, and GraphPipe, alongside attention work such as FlashMask and WLB-LLM. It explicitly credits disaggregation and graph decomposition as foundations and concentrates its distinction on frozen status and non-causal workload balancing. This goes beyond citation or bibliographic updates.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, and much of the explanatory narrative are rewritten. Related work is integrated into the background, motivation becomes a separate section, and model and context parallelization receive separate sections. The programming interface and detailed BAM explanation move to appendices, substantially changing the document's organization.

P2.justification: v3 redraws architecture and scheduling diagrams, adds memory-accounting and intra-GPU diagrams, and introduces compute-unit activity plots. End-to-end results become consolidated iteration-time panels, and context tables distinguish attention-layer and whole-model timings. The BAM illustration is revised and relocated, while extensive configuration tables disappear. Typography and running headers also change.

improvement.justification: v3 strengthens v1's GPU-level timing argument through component ablations, compute-unit traces, and the multistream alternative, while FSDP2 and GraphPipe* make the comparisons more informative. These gains are tempered by lost parallelism configurations and repetition reporting. Some conclusions also overgeneralize: Appendix D reports 16k LLM-S whole-model time of 705.14 ms for combined balancing versus 691.22 ms for intra-only balancing. The stronger mechanism evidence supports a modest net improvement, with reproducibility and qualification still weakened.
